message.content: The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is a small, early mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago. It belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, the ancestral lineage that gave rise to the orders Carnivora (to which lions belong) and Perissodactyla (to which zebras belong). In other words, the most recent common ancestor of these two species was a basal Laurasiatherian mammal that predated the split between the carnivores and the odd‑toed ungulates.
